question: How long is log data retained on the Team plan?
reference_answer: 15 days.

question: If I downgrade my plan, what happens to my old data?
reference_answer: Data older than the new plan's retention is deleted at the end of the billing period and cannot be recovered.

question: How do I verify that a webhook really came from Nimbus?
reference_answer: Check the X-Nimbus-Signature header: HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body with the webhook secret.

question: Is SAML SSO available on the Team plan?
reference_answer: No, SAML SSO is Enterprise only.

question: How do I reduce the number of notifications when many hosts alert at once?
reference_answer: Enable Group notifications on the multi-alert monitor.

question: How many widgets can a dashboard have?
reference_answer: At most 60.

question: What roles are available for workspace members?
reference_answer: Admin, Editor, Viewer and Billing.

question: How long before a certificate expires does the certificate monitor alert?
reference_answer: 14 days by default, configurable from 1 to 60 days.

question: How long are audit log events kept?
reference_answer: 90 days on Team, 13 months on Enterprise; Free has no audit log.

question: What is the acknowledgment timeout in an escalation policy?
reference_answer: 15 minutes by default, then the next level is notified.

question: Which metric types does the agent's StatsD server support?
reference_answer: Counter, gauge, histogram and set.

question: What service credit can I claim if uptime falls below the commitment?
reference_answer: 10% of the monthly fee below 99.9% and 25% below 99.0%, claimed within 30 days.

question: My phone keeps buzzing all night while we do planned work on our Postgres cluster. How can I make it stop without switching the checks off?
reference_answer: Create a maintenance window scoped by tag; monitors keep evaluating but notifications are silenced.

question: The status keeps bouncing between red and green every couple of minutes. How do I calm it down?
reference_answer: Set a recovery threshold lower than the alert threshold.

question: We'd like to be warned before a volume runs out of room rather than after it happens.
reference_answer: Use a forecast monitor, for example alert when a disk is predicted to fill within 48 hours.

question: One machine in the pool is behaving strangely compared with its siblings. Can that be spotted automatically?
reference_answer: Yes, with an outlier monitor.

question: Only wake someone up if failures are spiking and nobody is rolling out a release at that moment.
reference_answer: Use a composite monitor such as A && !B.

question: A colleague quit and now our scripts that talk to Nimbus are broken. How do we prevent that next time?
reference_answer: Issue API keys from a service account instead of tying automation to a person.

question: Can I let a client look at one of our boards, read-only, without creating a login for them?
reference_answer: Yes, with a public link; it expires after 30 days.

question: We are paying far too much for the text our applications write. What is the cheapest way to bring that down?
reference_answer: Add exclusion filters; excluded logs do not count toward indexed volume.

question: Is there a way to probe our admin site, which can't be reached from outside the office network?
reference_answer: Run a private location inside the network (Enterprise plan).

question: We told you we were leaving and still got billed again the month after. Why?
reference_answer: Usage in the final billing period is invoiced on the 1st of the following month.

question: Which destinations do I have to open on our outbound filtering for the monitoring software to work?
reference_answer: The ranges published in ranges.json.

question: Who edited this alert last week?
reference_answer: Open the monitor's History and select a version to see who made the change.

question: The person on duty didn't react to the page. What happens next?
reference_answer: After the acknowledgment timeout (15 minutes by default) the next level is notified.

question: The machines that run the Kubernetes API server don't show up in our host list.
reference_answer: Add tolerations so the DaemonSet schedules onto tainted control-plane nodes.

question: The numbers for how many copies of each workload are running are missing from our cluster view.
reference_answer: Enable the cluster agent with clusterAgent.enabled: true.

question: A value we just started using for our environment label can't be picked in the drop-down at the top of the board yet.
reference_answer: New tag values can take up to 10 minutes to appear in template variables.

question: Why did our usage explode after we began labelling every measurement with the customer's e-mail address?
reference_answer: Each new tag value creates a new series; do not use unbounded values as tags.

question: The uptime probe keeps crying wolf because of one flaky vantage point.
reference_answer: Alert only when 2 or more locations fail, and retry once before failing.

question: Do you keep information belonging to European customers inside Europe?
reference_answer: Yes, eu1 data is stored in the EU and never copied between regions.

question: The customer says they are thinking of moving to a competitor. Who needs to be told?
reference_answer: Tell the account's CSM.

question: How much money can I give back to an unhappy customer on my own authority?
reference_answer: A goodwill credit of up to USD 500 per incident; more needs the billing lead.

question: What does NM-4012 mean?
reference_answer: Timestamp too old: points older than 4 hours are rejected.

question: The agent log shows NM-4020. What is wrong?
reference_answer: Timestamps more than 10 minutes in the future; check time zone and hardware clock.

question: What does error NM-4021 mean and how do I fix it?
reference_answer: Clock skew over 60 seconds; enable time synchronization and restart the agent.

question: Why am I getting NM-4022?
reference_answer: Invalid metric name.

question: NM-2012 appears every few minutes in agent.log
reference_answer: An integration check exceeded check_timeout_s and was cancelled.

question: How do I get rid of NM-2102?
reference_answer: Give the agent access to the container runtime socket.

question: How do I fix NM-1004?
reference_answer: Set ca_bundle_path to a bundle containing the proxy's root certificate.

question: What is NM-5013?
reference_answer: Workspace suspended for non-payment.

question: What does NM-7002 mean?
reference_answer: Notification channel disabled after 50 consecutive failed deliveries.

question: What triggers NM-6011?
reference_answer: A query that would return more than 5,000 series.

question: What does NM-5001 mean?
reference_answer: The ingestion key belongs to another region; change the endpoint.

question: What does buffer_max_age_s do?
reference_answer: Maximum age of buffered data, default 1800 seconds; older data is discarded.

question: What is the default for flush_interval_s?
reference_answer: 10 seconds.

question: What does check_timeout_s control?
reference_answer: Maximum run time of one integration check, default 15 seconds.

question: When do I need hostname_override?
reference_answer: When several machines share a hostname, such as cloned VMs.

question: What is tls_min_version?
reference_answer: Lowest TLS version the agent negotiates, default 1.2.

question: What does nimbusctl buffer purge --older-than do?
reference_answer: Deletes buffered entries older than the given duration; they are never sent.

question: What does --dry-run do with nimbusctl check run?
reference_answer: Runs the check once and prints its metrics without sending them.

question: Is the output of nimbusctl config show --redact safe to share?
reference_answer: Yes, the ingestion key and proxy password are masked.

question: What is KI-219?
reference_answer: False failures from the Sydney synthetic location.

question: Agents in our EU workspace log NM-1001
reference_answer: EU workspaces must use ingest.eu1.nimbus-monitor.example.

question: Windows hosts have gaps in metrics and log NM-4021
reference_answer: Clock skew; enable the Windows Time service and restart NimbusAgent.

question: A customer's ingestion backlog has been growing for 20 minutes. What should I do?
reference_answer: Run the redrive-partition job from the admin console; escalate to ingest on-call past 30 minutes.

question: Our webhook signature check always fails even with the correct secret
reference_answer: Compute the HMAC over the raw request body, not re-serialized JSON.

question: A customer leaked an API key on GitHub. What is the process?
reference_answer: Force revoke the key, pull 30 days of audit logs, page sec-oncall.

question: Customer is on agent 3.3.1 and sees NM-2010 over and over
reference_answer: Known memory leak in 3.3.0 to 3.3.2 with container_discovery; upgrade to 3.3.3 or 3.4, or raise memory_limit_mb to 512 as a stopgap.

question: How do the request limits of API v1 and v2 differ?
reference_answer: v2: 600 per minute per workspace with Retry-After. v1: 300 per minute per key, no Retry-After.

question: We are moving from Collector 2.x to agent 3.4. What changes for proxy configuration?
reference_answer: 2.x read HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY; 3.x ignores them and needs proxy_url in agent.yaml.

question: Customer disputes their billed host count and wants money back
reference_answer: Export the hourly host report and show the p99 hour; credits up to USD 500, more needs the billing lead.

question: How many custom metrics are included and what happens when we go over?
reference_answer: 100 series per billed host, pooled; overage is billed on paid plans and dropped on Free (NM-4040).

question: The audit shows the leaked key was used from an unknown network. What now?
reference_answer: Revoke everything created with the key, open a P1 security incident, security lead notifies Admins within 72 hours.

question: Why can't I upgrade agent 2.8 to 3.4 with apt?
reference_answer: Agents older than 3.0 can't be upgraded in place; reinstall.

question: Can support temporarily raise a customer's API rate limit?
reference_answer: Yes, up to 2x for 72 hours with the api_rate_limit_override flag.

question: The agent ignores my HTTPS_PROXY environment variable. How do I configure a proxy?
reference_answer: Set proxy_url in agent.yaml.

question: What is the API rate limit and what happens when I exceed it?
reference_answer: 600 requests per minute per workspace; HTTP 429 with Retry-After.

question: Which Kubernetes version does the Helm chart need?
reference_answer: 1.26 or newer.

question: How do I install the agent on Ubuntu?
reference_answer: Run the install script with NIMBUS_KEY set.

question: Which HTTP header carries the API key?
reference_answer: Authorization: Bearer <key>.

question: How long can alerts be silenced for planned work?
reference_answer: A maintenance window can last up to 7 days and can recur.

question: Where is the agent's configuration file on Windows?
reference_answer: C:\ProgramData\Nimbus\agent.yaml.

question: How do I page through list results in the API?
reference_answer: Pass next_cursor as the cursor parameter; 100 items per page.

question: Can support temporarily raise a customer's API rate limit?
reference_answer: Public docs only say Enterprise plans can request higher limits.

question: How do I stop getting paged during a planned database upgrade?
reference_answer: Create a maintenance window scoped by tag.

question: How do I produce a diagnostics bundle from the agent?
reference_answer: Run nimbusctl diagnose --bundle.

question: How much credit can I get for an outage?
reference_answer: SLA credits of 10% or 25% depending on uptime (Enterprise).
